title: Interleaving Commands: a Threat to the Interoperability of Smartcard Based Security Applications
review_status: full-text audit complete; experimentally demonstrated silent command-interleaving anomalies on two smartcards
sections_checked: two-card Crypto Probing System experimental setup
evidence_note: Two commercially available smartcards from different manufacturers are tested. Interleaved APDUs can be accepted and signing workflows may terminate without warning; one other sequence contains modified/undefined commands. Demonstrates a concrete interoperability failure mode, not prevalence or real-world exploitation rate.

title: The RAppArmor Package: Enforcing Security Policies in R Using Dynamic Sandboxing on Linux
review_status: full-text audit complete; Linux/AppArmor sandbox proof-of-concept and selected security unit tests
sections_checked: security unit-test appendix and concluding remarks
evidence_note: RAppArmor uses OS-level AppArmor profiles and resource limits; appendix demonstrates selected blocked file-access, resource-exhaustion, and fork-bomb cases. Author explicitly calls the package a proof of concept, not a general solution. Linux-specific and dependent on policy quality; no comprehensive escape-rate or performance evaluation.

title: Secure Logical Schema and Decomposition Algorithm for Proactive Context Dependent Attribute Based Access Control
review_status: full-text audit complete; conditional formal non-inference guarantee; deployment evaluation proposed as future work
evidence_note: For given logical schema, functional dependencies, and correctly supplied sensitive attribute sets, a theorem establishes that decomposition blocks inference of those specified associations. The work proposes DBMS-facing verification modules as future applications; no production implementation, query overhead, or user evaluation is reported.

title: An Empirical Comparison of Dependency Network Evolution in Seven Software Packaging Ecosystems
review_status: full-text audit complete; historical observational dependency-graph study, not attack/vulnerability measurement
sections_checked: seven-ecosystem selection and Libraries.io data extraction
evidence_note: Compares Cargo, CPAN, CRAN, npm, NuGet, Packagist and RubyGems using package metadata up to April 2017. Finds ecosystem growth, concentrated updates and differing transitive-dependency fragility. Removed packages may be missing and vendored/dynamic dependencies are excluded. Measures graph structure, not compromise prevalence or security incidents.
